These are separate experiments. The website selects completed Python histories; it does not rerun Python in the browser. Each module preserves its own assumptions and accounting boundary.

Angkor · Temple relief · Angkor · Flight and refuge · Angkor · Maintenance repaired · Angkor · Labour and food accounts

Temple relief has four single trials. Flight has 320 histories. Repaired maintenance and the accounting extension each have 240 histories. The four modules contain 804 histories in total.

Timing repair

The original maintenance-only case reduced effort from year zero. The repaired case begins in year 55, as its README intended. With drought, its final state-linked population median changes from 3,296 to 6,209; the stable reference remains 6,958.

The accounting extension adds population-dependent farm labour, paid service rations and a separate refuge food ledger. Annual population, grain and labour balances pass. All added rates are experimental assumptions.

With drought, the extension’s median state-linked populations are 9,829 with maintained canals, 8,322 with reduced maintenance and 4,918 with elite reshuffling. The reshuffle bundles extraction, relief, trust and maintenance changes.

Higher military allocation can improve household food access through service rations in this extension. It has no battles or frontier logistics, so this is not a finding about military success.

Published economic foundation

The uploaded PDF is Klassen, Ortman, Lobo and Evans’s Provisioning an Early City. Its Table 5 gives a population–output-index exponent of 1.227, plus separate distance relationships. The live foundation module implements these relationships. The output index is constructed from labour, land and irrigation proxies; it is not measured rice tonnage.
